subject.title: [security] Tencent Cloud redirects can disclose session tokens and cloud-init credentials

question: Should Tencent Cloud API requests be made fail-closed for every redirect that leaves the initiating origin, including subdomains and effective-port changes?
rationale: The narrow security boundary is clear, but maintainers must explicitly accept the compatibility behavior for callers that currently rely on provider-endpoint redirects.

options.title: Adopt strict origin confinement
options.body: Reject any redirect whose scheme, canonical hostname, or effective port differs from the initiating Tencent API request, while preserving a stricter caller policy.

options.title: Retain default redirect behavior
options.body: Accept the documented credential-replay exposure and rely on Tencent endpoint integrity plus caller-supplied HTTP-client policies.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict origin confinement
recommendation.body: Reject any redirect whose scheme, canonical hostname, or effective port differs from the initiating Tencent API request, while preserving a stricter caller policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter has supplied the most concrete current-source security analysis and validation design available in this review.
